📝 Walkthrough ## Walkthrough This PR adds multi-region support, account management, native handoff flows, a Swift client SDK, database schema date transformations, and comprehensive documentation updates to AuthFn and DataFn. New region lookup adapters (Cloudflare Durable Objects, DynamoDB), an admin module for user management, account deletion with cascading cleanup, account-linking policies, and support for configurable session modes are implemented across the core and plugins. DataFn documentation is restructured with a new getting-started guide. ## Changes **AuthFn Region Lookup Adapters** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Cloudflare Durable Object region lookup store adapter**

`authfn/admin/src/index.ts`, `authfn/admin/package.json`, `authfn/admin/tsconfig.json`, `authfn/admin/vitest.config.ts`|Exports `createAuthFnAdmin` and route factories for listing users (cursor-paginated), deleting by id, and deleting by email (with ambiguity handling); wires authorization hooks, envelope handling, and parameter validation.| |**Admin operations and tests**
`authfn/admin/src/__tests__/admin.test.ts`|Comprehensive test suite covering authorization enforcement, cursor pagination with deterministic ordering, cascading hard-delete across users/sessions/credentials/profiles, multi-region lookup cleanup via `deleteByIdentifier`, and duplicate-email conflict handling with `deleteAllMatches` flag.| **AuthFn Regional Client & Multi-Region Support** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Regional client implementation**

Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks

Greptile Summary

This PR ports the AuthFn authentication system to the `dev` branch, adding multi-region routing with Cloudflare DO and DynamoDB lookup adapters, account-linking for password and OTP sign-up, a new admin router with per-operation authorization, native↔web session handoff, a Svelte session store, and a Swift client SDK. - **Core auth**: region lookup is now backed by a pluggable `lookupStore` with a caching layer; `buildLookupResult` now returns `continueLocally: true` instead of throwing when no region entry exists, enabling first-time sign-ups to proceed on the current region. - **New packages**: `@authfn/adapters/lookup-cloudflare-do` and `@authfn/adapters/lookup-dynamodb` implement the `AuthFnRegionLookupStore` contract; `@authfn/admin` adds an extensible admin router with configurable authorization callbacks and a static-key authorizer helper. - **Plugin hooks**: a new `hookFailurePolicy` mechanism lets plugins mark after-hooks as `'fail'` (propagating errors) rather than the default `'observe'` (fail-open); the multi-region plugin uses this to roll back sign-ups when region registration fails.

Confidence Score: 4/5

Safe to merge with one fix in the DynamoDB adapter before it handles production traffic. The DynamoDB adapter's `fromItem` function falls back to the sort-key constant `'LOOKUP'` when `regionId` is absent, silently corrupting region routing rather than surfacing an error. The rest of the surface area looks sound. authfn/adapters/lookup-dynamodb/src/index.ts (`fromItem` regionId fallback); authfn/admin/src/index.ts (`safeEqual` constant-time comparison).

Security Review

 - **`authfn/admin/src/index.ts` — `safeEqual` is not fully constant-time**: the byte-length comparison short-circuits before the XOR loop, leaking whether the submitted token has the correct byte length. This reduces the search space for brute-force guessing of the static admin token. Prefer `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (padding both buffers to equal length first).

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
